Chris Evert. An American tennis legend who won eighteen Grand Slam singles titles with a dominant baseline game built on exceptional consistency and precision. Her legendary rivalry with Martina Navratilova defined women's tennis in the 1970s and 1980s, and her seven French Open titles remain a testament to her clay-court mastery. She won two Australian Opens, seven French Opens, three Wimbledons, and six US Opens across her distinguished career. Known for her baseline game, exceptional consistency, and especially her forehand drive, her mental toughness and competitive spirit were legendary. She reached world number one in 1975 and held it for 260 weeks, dominating women's tennis from the early 1970s through the 1980s and establishing herself as a generational force. She won 1,309 professional matches, the most by any female player in history, with a seventy-five percent win rate, an extraordinary and nearly unmatched achievement of durability and skill. Her seven French Open titles showcase her clay-court dominance, and she reached the French Open final thirteen times across her career. She played over 150 times against Martina Navratilova, their rivalry spanning sixteen years, with each winning roughly half their encounters in a remarkably balanced competition. This combination of Grand Slam success, consistency, professional match victories, and dominant rivalry established her as one of tennis's all-time greats.
